modelAnswer: Reverse osmosis is a process in which external pressure greater than osmotic pressure is applied to a solution, forcing water molecules to move from the concentrated solution (higher solute concentration) to the dilute solution (lower solute concentration) through a semipermeable membrane, thereby reversing the natural direction of osmosis. One important application of reverse osmosis is the **desalination of seawater** to produce fresh drinking water for human consumption and agricultural use.

modelAnswer: Swelling of dead bones in water is due to osmosis. Dead bones contain collagen (a protein) and other organic materials in their matrix. When bones are placed in water, water molecules move into the bone structure through osmosis, as the solute concentration inside the bone is higher than outside. This causes the bone to absorb water and swell. The process occurs because the semipermeable nature of the bone matrix allows water to pass through while restricting the movement of larger solute molecules.

modelAnswer: The phenol-water system is a binary liquid mixture that exhibits partial miscibility at room temperature, forming two separate liquid phases. The upper consolute temperature (or upper critical solution temperature, UCST) is the maximum temperature above which phenol and water become completely miscible in all proportions, forming a single homogeneous phase. Below this temperature, the system separates into two liquid layers: one rich in phenol and one rich in water. This phenomenon occurs because hydrogen bonding between phenol and water molecules weakens at higher temperatures, allowing complete mixing.
